title: Viral ‘Beijing hit list’ targeting prominent Tibetans likely ‘fake’
author: Phayul Newsdesk
content:
Tenzin Nyidon
DHARAMSHALA, July 31:
A document circulating widely on social media, purportedly a confidential Chinese government directive ordering the surveillance of prominent Tibetans living overseas under China’s newly enacted so-called
Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress
, is exhibiting numerous indicators that call its authenticity into serious question.
The document, promoted online as a secret “Beijing hit list” or “target list,” claims Chinese authorities have instructed officials to monitor prominent Tibetan figures abroad. According to the document, those purportedly listed include Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) President Penpa Tsering; Tenzin Taklha, long-time aide to His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama; 11th Kirti Rinpoche Lobsang Tenzin Jigme Yeshe Gyamtso Rinpoche of Kirti Monastery; CTA Health Minister Pema Tso; and Tibetan educational sociologist Dr. Gyal Lo, who is widely known for exposing China’s state-run boarding school system in Tibet.
However, despite naming several prominent Tibetans, the document lacks virtually every defining characteristic of an authentic Chinese government directive.
Among the most conspicuous irregularities is the absence of an issuing government agency, an official document reference number, a date of issuance, an official seal, an approving authority, and an authorized signature. It also lacks a designated recipient, implementation instructions, or an identifiable administrative chain of command—elements standard in formal Chinese government communications.
Equally significant is the absence of an original, verifiable source. No official PDF, archival record, or independently authenticated version of the document has surfaced, making it impossible to establish its provenance.
The multilingual versions of the document also contain notable inconsistencies that undermine its credibility. In the Chinese text, the phrase used is “overseas Tibetan separatist elements,” whereas the accompanying English translation renders it as “Tibetan anti-China terrorists.” The term “terrorists” does not appear in the original Chinese wording, representing a substantial departure in meaning rather than a straightforward translation.
The document also employs an incorrect Chinese rendering of the name of CTA President Penpa Tsering, differing from the standardized form consistently used in official Chinese government publications. Such an error would be highly unusual in an authentic state-issued document referencing a well-known public figure. Taken together, these linguistic inconsistencies raise additional questions about whether the document originated from an official Chinese government source.
The circulation of seemingly official documents to amplify politically sensitive narratives is not unprecedented. In 2026, the exile Tibetan government known, officially as the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA), warned the public about a forged document bearing the official letterhead of the Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama. The fabricated document was circulated on Facebook to disseminate false information while mimicking the appearance of an authentic government communication.

title: More than 60 shave heads in New York to honour martyr Lobga Rangzen
author: Phayul Newsdesk
content:
Tenzin Nyidon
DHARAMSHALA, July 31:
More than 60 Tibetans living in exile participated in a symbolic head-shaving protest outside the United Nations headquarters in New York on Thursday to honour late Tibetan independence activist Lobga Rangzen and renew calls for international attention to Tibet’s unresolved political struggle.
Organized by the Regional Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) New York/New Jersey chapter, the memorial protest drew members of the Tibetan community who shaved their heads as a gesture of mourning, remembrance, and solidarity. The demonstration paid tribute to the late martyr, whose death has become a powerful symbol of sacrifice for many Tibetans advocating for Tibet’s freedom struggle movement.
Addressing the gathering, Regional TYC President Jamphel Choesang urged Tibetans to remain steadfast in carrying forward the aspirations of those who had sacrificed their lives for Tibet. “Our martyrs gave everything they had for Tibet. They did not sacrifice for themselves—they sacrificed for all of us, for future generations, and for the dream of a free and independent Tibet,” he said. “Their courage must never be forgotten, and their sacrifices must never be in vain.”
Remembering Lobga Rangzen, Choesang described his sacrifice as an appeal to awaken the world’s conscience and a reminder that the Tibetan struggle continues. “Our beloved Pawo Lobga Rangzen made the ultimate sacrifice to awaken the conscience of the world and to remind us that Tibet’s struggle is far from over. His message was clear: never give up on Tibet,” he said.
Calling for greater public participation, he encouraged Tibetans across the diaspora to actively support the movement through peaceful demonstrations and civic engagement. “Please stand up for our country. Join our protests whenever you can. Raise your voice for justice. Your presence matters,” he said, adding that every individual standing together sends “a powerful message that Tibet lives in our hearts and that we will never surrender our identity, our culture, or our dream of freedom.”
Emphasizing unity within the Tibetan community, he urged Tibetans to work together “as one family, one community, and one nation,” saying collective determination and mutual support remain among the movement’s greatest strengths.
“The responsibility to continue this movement belongs to every one of us,” he said. “Whether young or old, student or professional, every effort counts. Every protest, every prayer, every act of service, and every voice raised for Tibet keeps the flame of our martyrs burning brightly.”
The activist also appealed to the international community and the United Nations to recognize Lobga Rangzen’s sacrifice and respond to the aspirations of the Tibetan people. “We call upon the international community and the United Nations to hear the voices of the Tibetan people and to seek justice for Pawo Lobga Rangzen. His sacrifice deserves to be remembered, and the Tibetan people’s aspirations deserve to be heard,” he said.
Veteran Tibetan independence activist Lobga Rangzen self-immolated in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York on July 2.

title: Twin quakes measuring 5.7 and 5.8 jolt Drakkar County in Tibet’s Amdo region, triggers landslides
author: Phayul Newsdesk
content:
Tenzin Nyidon
DHARAMSHALA, July 28:
Twin earthquakes measuring 5.7 and 5.8 in magnitude struck Drakkar County in Tsolho (Ch. Hainan) Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture in Tibet’s Amdo region on Tuesday morning, triggering landslides and sending tremors across neighbouring areas.
According to the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC), the first earthquake struck at 11:16 a.m. local time, registering a magnitude of 5.7 with a focal depth of 10 kilometres. Just 18 minutes later, a second, slightly stronger 5.8-magnitude earthquake struck the same area at a similar depth.
Videos circulated by Chinese state media showed large plumes of dust billowing from mountain slopes, indicating landslides triggered by the powerful shaking. The tremors were reportedly felt in Xining, the capital of so called Qinghai Province, as well as in Lanzhou, the capital of neighbouring Gansu Province.
As of publication, there were no confirmed reports of fatalities, injuries, or collapsed buildings, although authorities continue to assess the impact in the affected area.
The twin earthquakes come amid growing concern among geologists and seismologists over heightened seismic activity across the Himalayan region, particularly the Tibetan Plateau. Earlier this year, on January 26, a magnitude 5.5 earthquake struck Thewo (Tewo) County in Kanlho (Gannan) Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture of Gansu Province at a depth of 10 kilometres, causing damage to several villages.
The Himalayan belt remains one of the world’s most seismically active regions due to the ongoing collision between the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates, making strong earthquakes a persistent geological hazard across Tibet and surrounding areas.

title: China orders eviction of monastics amid new demolition drive at Larung Gar
author: Phayul Newsdesk
content:
Tenzin Nyidon
DHARAMSHALA, July 28:
Chinese authorities have ordered monks and nuns whose residential quarters have been demolished at the renowned Larung Gar Buddhist Academy in Sertar County to leave the institute and return to their native monasteries, as Beijing presses ahead with its latest demolition campaign at one of the world’s largest centres of Tibetan Buddhist learning.
According to a report by the Dharamshala-based Tibetan outlet, Tibet Times, the order applies to all monastics whose residences have already been razed. Those from outside Serthar have been instructed to return either to their family homes or to monasteries in their native regions. At the same time, even monks and nuns originally from Serthar have reportedly been barred from remaining at Larung Gar and ordered to relocate to their local monasteries.
The latest measures follow a renewed demolition drive that began around
July 13, 2026.
Chinese authorities have justified the operation by claiming that the institute contains an excessive number of residential structures, creating safety concerns, and that the monastic population has grown beyond acceptable limits. Demolition crews have already torn down numerous residences, with the campaign continuing.
The current plan calls for the demolition of 1,060 monastic residences. Those whose quarters have been destroyed are no longer permitted to remain at Larung Gar and are being forcibly removed in successive groups.
Security restrictions across the academy have also been significantly tightened. Monks, nuns, and local residents are reportedly under heightened surveillance, while pilgrims and visitors from other areas are being prevented from entering the institute as authorities enforce stricter controls.
A source familiar with the developments told TT that Chinese authorities had initially planned to demolish the area surrounding Gyutrul Temple within the academy. However, monastery representatives reportedly appealed against the proposal, warning that such demolition would jeopardise the temple, the main assembly hall, and the circumambulation route. Following those representations, the authorities altered the plan and instead targeted the Joser residential quarters situated between the living areas of monks, nuns, and lay practitioners.
Larung Gar has been the target of repeated demolition campaigns over the past two decades. Chinese authorities carried out large-scale demolitions in 2001, 2016, and 2019, citing overcrowding and the absence of legally required construction permits. Those campaigns were also accompanied by stringent quotas on the resident monastic population and the forced removal of thousands of monks and nuns, particularly those who had travelled from other Tibetan regions to pursue Buddhist studies.
The 2019 demolition campaign also drew international attention after reports emerged that a nun, Tsering Dolma, died by suicide after leaving a final message describing how sustained state repression had driven her to despair.
Larung Gar, founded in 1980 by the late Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok, has long served as one of the most influential centres for the study of Tibetan Buddhism, attracting monks, nuns, and lay practitioners from across Tibet, China, and abroad. Human rights organisations and Tibetan groups have repeatedly criticised successive demolition campaigns and expulsions at the institute, arguing that they form part of broader efforts by the Chinese government to tighten control over Tibetan religious institutions and curtail independent monastic education.

title: TYC to open dedicated office in New York to counter Chinese disinformation on martyr Lobga Rangzen
author: Phayul Newsdesk
content:
Tenzin Nyidon
DHARAMSHALA, July 27:
As its Global Chain Hunger Strike entered its ninth day on Monday, the Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC), the largest pro-independence Tibetan organisation in exile, announced a new international campaign to counter what it described as Chinese disinformation surrounding the self-immolation of Tibetan independence activist Lobga Rangzen.
Addressing the media, TYC General Secretary Tenzin Lobsang said the organisation will establish a dedicated office in New York as part of its expanded advocacy efforts. The office will be led by former TYC Executive Committee members Dhondup Lhadar and Lamsang and will coordinate initiatives aimed at challenging disinformation and amplifying the Tibetan perspective internationally.
Calling for broad community participation, Lobsang urged Tibetans from all walks of life—including scholars, writers, researchers, artists, filmmakers, students, journalists, professionals, social media creators, and concerned citizens—to contribute through research, writing, public engagement, artistic works, videos, and advocacy.
He alleged that the Chinese government has been circulating false narratives portraying Lobga Rangzen as an unemployed individual whose sacrifice should not be taken seriously, while also depicting him as a product of Tibet’s former “feudal serfdom” system. The newly established office, he said, will serve as a platform to challenge such claims and ensure that the circumstances surrounding Lobga Rangzen’s sacrifice are accurately documented and remembered.
TYC Vice President Tashi Targyal stated that the movement, which originated in Dharamshala, has quickly evolved into a global campaign. Under the guidance of the organisation’s Central Executive Committee, solidarity hunger strikes and demonstrations have already been organised in Dalhousie, Kalimpong, Dekyiling, Kullu, Odisha, Rajpur, Tenzingang, and several other Tibetan settlements, with additional chapters and communities continuing to join the initiative.
“The Tibetan Youth Congress will continue to expand this Worldwide Chain Protest until the United Nations responds,” the organisation said in a statement. “We urge governments, international institutions, media organisations, and people of conscience across the world to pay attention, engage with the facts, and stand with the Tibetan people’s right to preserve their identity, dignity, and future.”
The initiative which began in Dharamshala on July 19, has so far drawn the participation of 64 individuals who sat for a one-day hunger strike on a rolling basis. On Monday, members of the Tibetan Market Association joined the relay hunger strike outside the Tibetan Market near the Main Tibetan Temple in McLeod Ganj, Dharamshala, in a show of solidarity with the ongoing campaign.
Members of the Tibetan Market Association participate in the relay hunger strike in Dharamshala on July 27, 2026 (Phayul photo)
The announcement comes a week after the TYC launched its Global Chain Hunger Strike following Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation outside the United Nations Headquarters in New York on July 2. Through the worldwide campaign, the organisation has put forward five key demands. These include a formal and substantive response from the United Nations to the circumstances surrounding Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation; the repeal of China’s so-called “Ethnic Unity and Progress Law”; international recognition of Tibet’s historical status and right to independence; accountability for China’s policies and alleged repression in Tibet; and the immediate and unconditional release of Tibetan political prisoners, including the 11th Panchen Lama.

title: Senior Chinese leader calls for full implementation of ethnic unity law during Tibet visit
author: Phayul Newsdesk
content:
Tenzin Nyidon
DHARAMSHALA, July 24:
Senior Chinese Communist Party (CCP) leader Wang Huning has called for the full implementation of China’s newly enacted “Ethnic Unity and Progress Law” during a four-day inspection tour of Tibet, while also urging local authorities to deepen the Sinicisation of Tibetan Buddhism and strengthen social governance in line with Beijing’s assimilation agenda.
Wang, a member of the CCP’s seven-member Politburo Standing Committee and chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference, visited Lhasa and Ngari Prefecture, an area bordering India and Nepal, from July 19 to 22. The visit comes just weeks after the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law came into force on 1 July, signalling Beijing’s determination to accelerate the implementation of legislation widely viewed as providing a legal basis for deeper assimilation, intensified ideological oversight, and expanded security governance across Tibet.
Throughout the visit, Wang reiterated Beijing’s longstanding governing principle that “to govern Tibet is foremost to stabilise Tibet.” He called on local authorities to preserve what he described as a political and social environment of unity and stability while ensuring the full implementation of the new ethnic unity legislation.
During a visit to a Tibetan Buddhist monastery, Wang renewed calls to “systematically promote the Sinicisation of religion,” stressing that Tibetan Buddhism must be further aligned with socialist values and the ideological priorities of the Chinese Communist Party.
“We must ensure the effective implementation of the Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress, improve the ability and level of governing ethnic affairs according to law, and promote the spirit of ethnic unity and progress in all areas of development. In accordance with the requirements of systematically promoting the Sinicisation of religion in our country and strengthening the rule of law in religious affairs, we must continuously guide Tibetan Buddhism to adapt to socialist society,” Wang said during the tour, according to Chinese state media.
State media also showed Wang examining a Ming dynasty imperial eulogy to the Buddhist canon, a historical artefact frequently invoked by Beijing to bolster its narrative that Tibet and Tibetan Buddhism have long been integral to successive Chinese dynasties and, by extension, the Chinese state.
Wang’s remarks come amid intensifying international criticism of China’s newly implemented ethnic unity law. In recent weeks, lawmakers and government representatives in the United States and the European Union have issued statements condemning the legislation, warning that it institutionalises forced assimilation under the guise of national unity and grants authorities sweeping powers to curb activities deemed harmful to “ethnic unity” or supportive of “separatism.”
Exile Tibetan leaders and advocacy groups have echoed those concerns, arguing that the law codifies assimilationist policies that threaten Tibet’s distinct cultural, linguistic, and religious identity while extending Beijing’s control over other non-Han regions. They contend that the legislation marks another significant step in China’s broader campaign to reshape Tibet and other occupied regions’ identities through legal, political, and ideological mechanisms.

title: Chinese Ambassador expresses dismay over seminar on Tibetan studies in Kathmandu
author: Phayul Newsdesk
content:
Tenzin Nyidon
DHARAMSHALA, July 23:
Chinese Ambassador to Nepal Zhang Maoming has expressed concern over the upcoming 17th Seminar of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (IATS), a leading international academic conference scheduled to take place in Kathmandu from August 23 to 29.
According to reports, Ambassador Zhang raised the matter during a meeting with Nepal’s Foreign Secretary, Amrit Bahadur Rai, on Tuesday. He reportedly conveyed Beijing’s concerns that the conference could become a platform for activities or statements that China regards as politically sensitive, particularly those relating to Tibet and the Tibetan spiritual leader, His Holiness the Dalai Lama.
The envoy reportedly urged the Nepali authorities to ensure that the seminar remains strictly within the realm of academic inquiry and is not used as a forum for political expression. While no formal diplomatic protest or request to cancel the event has been made, the concerns were conveyed verbally as part of ongoing diplomatic exchanges between the two countries.
Observers suggest that Beijing’s unease may have been heightened after the Nepali government permitted Tibetan refugees to publicly celebrate the 91st birthday of His Holiness the Dalai Lama earlier this month—an event that has traditionally faced official restrictions in Nepal.
Responding to the concerns, the seminar organizers rejected suggestions that the gathering carries a political agenda. “It’s not a pro-Dalai Lama event. A large number of Chinese professors and scholars are also attending. The Chinese Embassy is aware of the seminar. We have informed the relevant government agencies as well,” Prof. Sagar Sharma of Kathmandu University told
The Kathmandu Post.
Organizers emphasized that the International Association for Tibetan Studies is an independent academic organization dedicated to advancing scholarship on Tibetan history, language, religion, philosophy, literature, art, and culture. They stressed that the seminar is intended to foster rigorous academic dialogue and facilitate the exchange of research among scholars from across the globe.
The week-long conference is expected to attract hundreds of researchers and academics from nearly 40 countries, including participants from China. It will be jointly hosted by the Himalaya Centre for Asian Studies (HiCAS) at Kathmandu University and the Kathmandu University Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute (KU-CBS at RYI). According to the IATS website, the seminar is being convened by Prof. Sagar Sharma of HiCAS and Prof. Thomas Doctor of KU-CBS at RYI.
Founded at the University of Oxford in 1979, the International Association for Tibetan Studies is a non-political scholarly organization devoted to promoting research on Tibetan history, religion, linguistics, literature, philosophy, and the arts. Its seminars, held every three years in different host countries, are widely regarded as the foremost international forum for academic research on Tibet.

title: China imposes heavy security, tightens surveillance in Lobga Rangzen’s hometown
author: Phayul Newsdesk
content:
Tenzin Nyidon
DHARAMSHALA, July 23:
Chinese authorities have reportedly imposed sweeping security measures in the Lower Zako region in Ganzi (Kardze) Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Kham, the hometown of late Tibetan independence activist Lobga Rangzen, according to information obtained by Phayul from a member of the Sino-Tibet dialogue platform Lhasa Spring, who requested anonymity due to security concerns.
The source told Phayul that armed personnel from China’s National Security and Public Security agencies have maintained a heavy presence in the area since early July, with residents’ movements and communications have been placed under strict restrictions. The situation has left the township under intense surveillance, while local people are reportedly living under constant monitoring and fear amid the continued security crackdown.
Earlier this month,
Lobga Rangzen
set himself on fire in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York and later succumbed to his injuries. A Tibetan refugee based in New York, he worked as a taxi driver. He escaped to exile in India in 1992, where he later pursued monastic studies at Ganden Monastery in southern India. His entire family still resides in Tibet.
According to the source, security forces, including personnel from China’s National Security and Public Security agencies, entered the area shortly after July 2, following Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation. Since then, the village has remained under heightened surveillance, with residents subjected to stringent controls aimed at preventing any potential unrest.
“The area has been controlled tightly,” the source told Phayul. “We are trying to establish contact with them.” The source added that fear has spread among local residents, making it nearly impossible to obtain information about Lobga Rangzen’s family members and relatives.
“For his family, we don’t know what has happened,” the source said. “Local people are afraid to visit them. They told me they don’t even dare to call them because they are being guarded and are under the watch of National Security.”
As of publication, the whereabouts and condition of Lobga Rangzen’s family members remain unknown. The source said efforts to reach them have so far been unsuccessful due to the extensive security restrictions imposed in the area.
The reported security crackdown reflects a pattern frequently documented by rights groups, in which Chinese authorities intensify surveillance and impose collective restrictions on the family members and hometowns of Tibetans who engage in political activism abroad. While the precise situation facing Lobga Rangzen’s family could not be independently verified, sources indicate that the area remains under tight security, with communications and travel severely curtailed.

title: Dalai Lama congratulates Andy Burnham on becoming UK Prime Minister
author: Phayul Newsdesk
content:
Tenzin Nyidon
DHARAMSHALA, July 21:
Tibetan leader His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama has written to Andy Burnham to congratulate him on assuming office as the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, extending his best wishes and expressing hope that his leadership will contribute to peace, compassion, and international cooperation during a period of global uncertainty.
In his congratulatory message, the Tibetan spiritual leader emphasised that the world is currently facing profound challenges that demand collective action and responsible leadership. Recalling the United Kingdom’s longstanding role on the international stage, he expressed confidence that Prime Minister Burnham would not only work for the welfare and prosperity of the British people but also collaborate closely with other nations to address pressing global issues.
The nonagenarian leader also reflected on the enduring relationship between Tibetans and the United Kingdom, describing it as historic and distinctive. “As you may be aware, we Tibetans have long enjoyed a historic and unique relationship with your country,” he wrote. “During my several visits there, I have deeply appreciated the warmth extended to me by people from all walks of life, as well as their support for my efforts to promote human values, nonviolence, and interfaith harmony.”
Concluding his message, His Holiness wished the new British leader success in fulfilling the hopes and aspirations of the British people while contributing to a more peaceful and compassionate world.
Andy Burnham assumed office as the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom on July 20, 2026, succeeding Keir Starmer, who stepped down following mounting domestic political pressures and the Labour Party’s disappointing performance in local elections. Burnham has pledged to prioritize a policy agenda centered on devolving greater powers to local authorities, revitalizing regional industries, and tackling the country’s persistent cost-of-living crisis.
Burnham secured the Labour Party leadership in a decisive internal contest, earning overwhelming backing from Labour Members of Parliament. With Labour commanding a parliamentary majority, his election as party leader automatically elevated him to the premiership, eliminating the need for a nationwide general election. His appointment makes him the seventh individual to occupy 10 Downing Street within the past decade.
Before becoming Prime Minister, Burnham served as the widely respected Mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to 2026. He returned to the House of Commons in June 2026 as the Member of Parliament for Makerfield after winning a by-election, a move that positioned him to contest the Labour leadership. Earlier in his political career, he held several senior Cabinet portfolios under former Prime Ministers Tony Blair and Gordon Brown, including serving as Secretary of State for Health from 2009 to 2010.

title: Two Tibetan youth trafficked to Myanmar in fake job scam, families face ransom demand
author: Phayul Newsdesk
content:
Tenzin Nyidon
DHARAMSHALA, July 21:
Two young Tibetan men from Palyul County in Kardze, eastern Tibet, have reportedly been trafficked into a Chinese-run cyber scam compound in Myanmar after being lured by fraudulent job offers, according to the Dharamshala-based Tibetan radio station, Voice of Tibet (VoT).
The criminal network has now demanded a ransom exceeding 500,000 yuan (approximately US$73,000) from their families, threatening that failure to pay would mean the two men would not be released alive.
A source familiar with the incident said the scam primarily targets educated young people, particularly recent university graduates seeking employment. Recruiters allegedly entice victims with promises of high-paying jobs before funnelling them into criminal networks operating in Myanmar.
The two young men were allegedly deceived by a Tibetan woman who assured them they would receive attractive salaries and perform relatively easy work. She reportedly escorted them to Yunnan Province, where they were handed over to operators of a Chinese-run cyber scam compound in Myanmar.
The case reflects a broader trafficking network that has expanded rapidly in recent years. Chinese-run cyber scam syndicates have reportedly recruited and deceived thousands of young people from countries including India, Nepal, China, and Vietnam before transporting them to scam compounds along Myanmar’s border.  Victims are often deceived with offers of well-paid technology or office-based jobs before being trafficked across borders and forced to participate in online fraud operations. Once inside these compounds, victims are reportedly subjected to coercion, harsh living conditions, and forced to carry out online financial fraud while their families face extortion demands.
The two Tibetans recently fell victim to such a scheme, triggering deep concern among their families and members of the Tibetan community familiar with the case.
The latest case involving the two young Tibetans highlights the increasing sophistication of cross-border trafficking networks that exploit the aspirations of young job seekers through deceptive recruitment, only to subject them to exploitation and extortion once they arrive in Myanmar’s cyber scam compounds.

title: Public Service Commission Begins Tibetan Language Workshop for CTA Settlement Office Secretaries
author: Palden Choedon
content:
Sarah: The Public Service Commission of the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) inaugurated a ten-day Tibetan Language Workshop for Tibetan Settlement Office staff this morning at College for Higher Tibetan Studies (CHTS), Sarah. The workshop has brought together 21 CTA officials currently serving as office secretaries in various Tibetan settlement offices in India and Nepal.

The inaugural ceremony was attended by Public Service Commissioner Karma Yeshi as the chief guest. Also present were CHTS Principal Passang Tsering, Public Service Commission Secretary Tenzin Legdup, and the workshop instructors, who are faculty members of the college. The programme commenced with the lighting of the traditional ceremonial butter lamp by Commissioner Karma Yeshi and Principal Passang Tsering.

Following the inauguration, the participating CTA officials introduced themselves, sharing their respective settlement offices and providing the gathering with an overview of their backgrounds.

Passang Tsering, Principal of CHTS, addressed the participants by highlighting the improvements made to the workshop facilities, the minor revisions to the course structure, and introducing the new batch of college faculty members assigned to conduct the sessions.

He underscored the importance of teaching and learning Tibetan history, noting the growing challenge posed by false narratives promoted by some Western Tibetologists. He stressed that individuals should be well-equipped with an accurate understanding of Tibetan history so they can confidently explain and uphold the truth whenever the need arises.

Speaking about the workshop’s objectives, he states that the Tibetan Language Workshop for Tibetan Settlement Offices is specifically designed to strengthen participants’ Tibetan language proficiency in relation to their current professional responsibilities. Unlike courses intended to prepare candidates for the CTA Civil Service Entrance Examination, the workshop aims to support the continuous development of Tibetan language skills throughout participants’ careers.

Public Service Commissioner, Karma Yeshi, emphasised that learning is a lifelong pursuit, drawing on the Buddhist belief that knowledge and wisdom benefit an individual not only in this life but also in future lives. He stressed the enduring value of continuous learning and self-improvement.

He spoke about the CTA staff Training Policy, which provides training at three different stages of a civil servant’s career. In this context, he highlighted the importance of Tibetan language proficiency, particularly in drafting official correspondence, and urged participants to pay close attention to the nuances of formal writing and avoid Tibetan spelling errors.

Encouraging participants to make the most of the programme, he urged them to reflect on what they had learned and assess how much they had improved by the end of the workshop. He also stressed the importance of overall personal development, including maintaining good handwriting, noting that such qualities are especially significant for settlement office secretaries and reflect both professionalism and personal discipline.

He further encouraged participants to openly share the experiences and challenges they encounter in their respective settlements among each other and to actively engage with the faculty by seeking clarification whenever they had questions or doubts.

Concluding his address, Karma Yeshi reflected on the current challenges facing the Tibetan cause and His Holiness the Dalai Lama’s advancing age. He reminded CTA civil servants to remain mindful of the sacrifices made by Tibetans, while encouraging them to take care of their health, preserve Tibetan culture and language, and carry out their responsibilities with dedication.

The ten-day workshop will comprise a total of 52 sessions covering Tibetan history, Tibetan grammar, official letter writing, lexicography, and phonetics.

title: Tibetans and Japanese Observe Unite for Tibet and Global Day of Action to Honour Martyr Lobga Rangzen in Tokyo
author: Palden Choedon
content:
Tokyo: The Students for Free Tibet Japan and the Tibetan Community in Japan organised a function and peace march yesterday to observe the Global Day of Action to remember and honour Martyr Lobsang Palden (Lobga Rangzen), who self-immolated before the United Nations building a month ago. Tibetans and Japanese supporters gathered at Jingu-dori Park carrying Tibetan national flags and posters of Lobsang Palden.

Dr. Tsewang Gyalpo Arya, Representative of the Liaison Office of H.H. the Dalai Lama for Japan and East Asia, briefed the participants on what this Global Day of Action is about and how Martyr Lobsang Palden self-immolated to protest the Chinese Ethnic Unity and Progress Law and to draw the United Nations and the international community’s attention to the Chinese heinous intention behind this Ethnic Unity Law. He urged all to remember Martyr Lobsang Palden’s words and protest the Ethnic Unity Law and the injustices happening in China and the occupied regions of Tibet, East Turkistan, Southern Mongolia and other regions.

Dorjee Shiota of the Tibetan Community in Japan and Tsering Dorjee of Students for Free Tibet Japan thanked the participants and called on all Tibetans to unite and work to fulfill the last wishes of Martyr Lobsang Palden by keeping the issue of Tibet alive. Tenzin Chodon of the Students for Free Tibet read the biography of Martyr Lobsang Palden.

After the function, the participants started the Peace March from Jingu-dori Park and marched around the busy Shibuya street, raising slogans for freedom and justice for Tibet, asking the United Nations to take action and urge the CCP regime to repeal the repressive law and send a fact-finding delegation to Tibet.

In the afternoon, a film show and panel discussion on the Self-immolation and the Ethnic Unity Law were organised at Tokyo University Komaba Complex. A two-hour 2015 documentary film “Lungta”, directed by Ikeya Kaoru, was screened, in which the Tibetans’ struggle in Tibet and in exile and the life story of some self-immolators were delineated. Director Ikeya, during the panel discussion, talked about his experience in working with the Tibetans and the compassionate culture of Tibet. He lamented that the Tibet issue has not received much attention lately and the Tibetans are forced to self-immolate to draw the international community’s attention.

Prof Ako Tomoko of the University of Tokyo moderated the panel discussion and talked about how Lobga Rangzen committed self-immolation before the UN building. She urged the international community to pay attention and do more in resolving the problems the Tibetans, Uyghurs, Southern Mongolians and other minority nationals are facing under the CCP regime.

Representative Dr. Tsewang Gyalpo Arya thanked the Director Ikeya and Nakahara for the film in which Tibetan struggle and self-immolation aspects have been conveyed succinctly. He thanked Prof. Ako for her cooperation in making this film and panel discussion possible at the university. Representative Arya briefly explained why Tibetans are forced to commit self-immolation and why Martyr Lobga Rangzen burnt himself before the United Nations building. He said the worsening human rights and religious repression in Tibet, and the silence of the international community and the implementation of China’s Ethnic Unity and Progress law as major reasons that forced Lobga Rangzen to self-immolate to protest the CCP regime and to draw the United Nations’ attention.

Tsering Dorjee of the Students for Tibet Japan spoke about China’s colonial boarding schools and how more than one million Tibetan children are forced into these boarding schools for indoctrination in communist ideology and are deprived of education in their mother tongue and religious culture.

Fujita Yoko of the Students for Free Tibet emceed the event. Participants posed many questions to the panels on: Ethnic Law, the situation in Tibet and other occupied nationals, colonial boarding schools, India and China relations, the Tibetan middle way approach, and so on. The film screening and the panel discussion took around four hours, exceeding the time limit. Around two hundred people participated in the event at Tokyo University.

Information booklets on the colonial boarding schools, Chinese interference in the selection of H.H. the Dalai Lama’s reincarnation, and Tibetan bulletins were distributed to the audience.

-Report filed by the Office of Tibet, Japan

title: Members of Parliament Geshe Lharampa Atuk Tseten and Lharong Successfully Complete Their Official Visit to Delhi
author: Dawa Tsering
content:
Dharamshala: As part of the program of the 18th Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, Parliamentarians Geshe Lharampa Atuk Tseten and Lharong successfully concluded their official visitation program with their final program in Delhi from 28 to 30 July, 2026.

On the morning of July 30 at 9:30 AM, the two Parliamentarians departed from Samyeling, Delhi, and visited the Bureau of His Holiness the Dalai Lama in Delhi. Upon arrival, Representative Jigme Tsering, the Secretary, and other staff members extended a warm welcome and presented a briefing on the office’s operations. The Parliamentarians first expressed their congratulations to the newly appointed Representative. They then provided guidance emphasizing the general status of the Indian Registration Certificate (RC) and the Identity Certificate (IC), stressing the need to exercise strict attention and diligence regarding these two documents, particularly for Tibetans residing in South India and Dharamshala.

At 12:30 PM, the Parliamentarians paid visits to local religious centers including Jangtse Lhamo Khang, Jangchup Lhakhang, and Drepung Ngagpa Dratsang, as well as administrative offices such as the Local Assembly, the Tibetan Medical & Astro-Institute, the Regional Tibetan Freedom Movement (BRDL), and the local Health Clinic. Later in the afternoon, they visited the Central Executive Office of Dokham Chushi Gangdruk, where General Secretary Karma Samdup and Treasurer Geshe Tenzin Ngodup introduced their ongoing initiatives aligned with the guidance of His Holiness the Dalai Lama before guiding a tour of the Heroes Memorial Hall.

At 5:00 PM, a public gathering was convened at the Samyeling Local Assembly Hall, Geshe Lharampa Atuk Tseten spoke on  the vast accomplishments of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, international geopolitics, and the unifying inspiration of patriot Rangzen Lobga self-immolation. He highlighted the nationwide support and campaigns sparked by this noble act of sacrifice, urging everyone across the three traditional provinces and religious sects to stand united and continue advocating for the Tibetan cause in accordance with the martyr’s hopes. While Parliamentarian Lharong addressed the critical situation inside Tibet, the official resolution of solidarity passed unanimously during the 1st session of the 18th Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile regarding the grave conditions in Tibet, and the critical dangers law posed by the Chinese Communist Government’s so-called “Ethnic Unity and Progress Law” which was enforced starting 1 July, 2026, designed to eradicate Tibet’s distinct religion, culture, language, and national identity, along with strategies to counter these policies.

Following the speeches, an open Q&A session was held. The Parliamentarians provided detailed responses and clarifications to questions and views expressed by the attendees, successfully concluding the gathering.

In the evening, 26 local associations hosted a farewell dinner for the visiting delegates, marking the official conclusion of all programs scheduled for the Delhi visit.

– Report filed by Tibetan Parliamentary Secretariat

title: A Global Appeal- Open letter from the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile On the People’s Republic of China’s Ethnic Unity and Progress Law
author: Dawa Tsering
content:
A Call to Defend Human Rights, Cultural Diversity, Religious Freedom, and the Peaceful Resolution of the Tibet-China Conflict

To: Heads of State and Government, Parliamentary Leaders and Members, the United Nations, Human Rights Organizations, Religious and Interfaith leaders and Friends of Tibet.

The Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile the democratically elected legislative institution representing the Tibetan people across the globe calls to act with urgency in response to the People’s Republic of China’s Ethnic Unity and Progress Law, which came into force on 1 July 2026. Presented as a measure to promote “national unity,” this law deepens policies that threaten the Tibetan people’s language, religion, culture, identity, and fundamental human rights.

The gravity of this moment was tragically underscored by the sacrifice of Tibetan activist Lobga Rangzen, who died after setting himself on fire outside the United Nations Headquarters in New York on 2nd July 2026. His final appeal was for a free Tibet where Tibetans can live with dignity, freedom, and the protection of their fundamental rights.

We respectfully call upon governments, parliaments, the United Nations, and the international community to:

A Defining Test of the International Human Rights System

The implementation of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law is not solely a Tibetan concern. It is a test of the international community’s commitment to protecting cultural diversity, freedom of religion or belief, linguistic rights, minority protections, and the rule of international human rights law.

When the identity of a people is threatened, the principles upon which the international human rights system is built are also put at risk.

The Tibetan people’s struggle has always been guided by truth, compassion, and non-violence. We believe that silence in the face of injustice only emboldens oppression. We therefore urge the international community to stand with the Tibetan people in defending human dignity, religious freedom, cultural diversity, and the universal values that unite us all.

Lasting peace cannot be achieved through forced assimilation. Lasting unity cannot be built by erasing identity. A stable and harmonious future can only be founded on respect for human dignity, cultural diversity, religious freedom, and meaningful dialogue

The future of Tibet should be shaped through dialogue—not assimilation; through justice—not coercion.

Dolma Tsering TeykhangDated: 1 August 2026SpeakerTibetan Parliament-in-ExileGangchen Kyishong, DharamshalaHimachal Pradesh, India

title: The Tibetan Institute of Performing Arts Concludes 4th Summer Tibetan Performing Arts Training Programme
author: Ngawang Tsepak
content:
Dharamshala: The Tibetan Institute of Performing Arts (TIPA) held the closing ceremony of its 4th Summer Tibetan Performing Arts Training Programme this morning at 10:30 a.m. in the institute’s auditorium. Secretary of the Department of Education Karma Choeying attended the ceremony as the chief guest. The event was also attended by the parents and family members of the participating students, along with TIPA staff members.

At the opening ceremony, the TIPA Director,Dhundup Tsering,welcomed the Chief guest and all the students, parents, and family members who had come specially from abroad to attend the closing ceremony. He spoke about TIPA’s objectives and noted that interest in Tibet’s unique performing arts among young Tibetans living abroad has been growing steadily. Since 2023, this training has been organised to coincide with the summer holidays of young Tibetans raised abroad. What began with around thirty students has now reached its fourth summer training programme.

During the training, teachers dedicated their full effort to teaching the students the Tibetan language as well as Tibetan opera arts, musical instruments, dance, and folk songs. Students were also encouraged to carry forward and promote Tibetan performing arts and their own identity when they return to their residence. Following this, the students who took part in the training performed around twelve different pieces, including song and dance performances, instrumental music, and traditional folk songs.

On this occasion, Chief guest Secretary Karma Choeying presented certificates and ceremonial scarves (khatags) to all the students who successfully completed the training programme. Addressing the gathering, he said it was encouraging to see the students show such keen interest in learning Tibetan performing arts and commended the parents for their unwavering support.

He also expressed appreciation to the TIPA instructor for their month-long commitment, under the Institute’s guidance, worked diligently for a month to teach the students song, dance, and instrumental performance, resulting in today’s excellent presentation. He noted that this work constitutes the preservation of Tibetan culture.

Referring to the challenges facing Tibet under Chinese rule, he stressed that safeguarding Tibetan religion, language, and culture remains essential to preserving Tibetan identity.

He also cited His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama’s quoting “hold on to hope while preparing for hardship”, noting that the Tibetan struggle is a shared responsibility. He said the responsibility for protecting Tibetan identity rests with every Tibetan, and that instilling the language, religion, and culture passed down from their ancestors into the hearts of young Tibetans must begin at home — if parents speak to their children in Tibetan and cultivate this habit, Tibetan identity can be protected and preserved.

The month-long training programme, organised by TIPA from1 July to 1 August 2026to coincide with the summer holidays of young Tibetans living abroad, concluded successfully, marking the completion of its fourth edition.

-Report filed by Tibetan Institute of Performing Arts

Bern — The Tibetan community in Switzerland and Liechtenstein has launched a week of peaceful rally and solidarity walk from the Swiss Federal Parliament (Bundeshaus) in Bern to the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Zurich, from March 4 to 10, 2026. The aim is to raise public awareness of human rights issues in Tibet and to call the Chinese government for transparency, respect for human rights, and compliance with legal standards in Tibetan regions.

According to the Office of Tibet, Geneva, on March 4, 2026, the Tibetan Community of Switzerland and Liechtenstein has inaugurated a week-long peaceful rally and solidarity walk in Bern, they will walk till march 10th, 2026, the Tibetan National Uprising Day, from the Swiss Federal Parliament (Bundeshaus) in Bern to the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Zurich.

Around 15 participants, aged between the ages of 35 and 75, represent intergenerational commitment and unity. This event, based on non-violence, dignity, and constructive dialogue, aims to raise public awareness of humanitarian concerns in Tibet and call for transparency, respect for human rights, and compliance with legal standards in Tibetan regions.

Representative Thinley Chukki, the Office of Tibet, Geneva, addressed the participants at the launch and she saud,''Today, as we gather in front of the Swiss Parliament, I thank our guest of honour, a Member of Parliament, for inaugurating this peace march. This march coincides with the 90th birthday of His Holiness the Dalai Lama and seeks to draw global attention to the suffering of Tibetans in Tibet. Over one million Tibetan children face forced residential schooling, and in 2024 alone, around 650,000 Tibetans were effected by the forced labour programmes according to the UN reports. Infrastructure projects and dams have displaced nearly one million Tibetans, depriving them of their livelihoods."

"We call on the international community to recognise these violations and extend their support. I thank all participants for dedicating seven days of their lives to this cause. May our efforts advance freedom in Tibet, a peaceful resolution of the Sino-Tibetan conflict, and the long life of His Holiness the Dalai Lama," she added.

Katharina Prelicz-Huber, Member of the National Council of Switzerland, expressed her support, conveying the solidarity of the Tibetan Parliamentary Group and providing a message to be delivered on 10 March, 2026, marking the 67th anniversary of the Tibetan National Uprising Day. The letter was signed by co-presidents Councillor of States Diana Moser, National Councillor Leonore Borges, National Councillor Nick Gucker, National Councillor Fabian Molina, and Maya Graf, Councillor of States.

According to the report, beyond Tibet, the march carries a universal message: in a world affected by war, conflict, and human suffering, peace, dialogue, and non-violence remain essential. Inspired by His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, the Tibetan Community emphasises that lasting solutions come through respect, understanding, and peaceful negotiation.

They said that the march from Bern to Zurich stands as both a call for justice in Tibet and a symbolic gesture of solidarity with all peoples affected by war and instability worldwide.

New Delhi — The Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) organised a strong protest outside the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in New Delhi on June 7, 2026. The demonstrators protested against the Chinese government's ongoing political repression in Tibet and the implementation of the so-called "ethnic unity" law, while also paying tribute to the sacrifice of Tibetan patriot Lobga Rangzen, who sacrificed his life for the cause of Tibet.

The Tibetan Youth Congress also sent an open letter to the Embassy of People's Republic of China in New Delhi on the same day and they said,"This is not merely a letter. It is a message carried by the final sacrifice of Tibetan patriot Lobga Rangzen, whose body was engulfed in flames because our homeland had been occupied and our people deprived of their freedom. His last act was not one of despair, it was one of resistance. he raised the Tibetan National Flag and he stood on fire, and declared to the world: "Free Tibet, China Out of Tibet."

"Rangzen Lobga sacrificed his life because, he view that the root cause of the Tibetan tragedy is simple: China occupied our country, we lost our independence and the continued political control exercised by the so-called People's Republic of China over Tibet. He sacrificed himself for the cause of Tibet and its Independence because decades of political repression, cultural destruction, restrictions on religious freedom, transnational repression, and now the implementation of the so-called "Ethnic Unity Law."

"You call it a law of unity. In reality you are trying to legalize the genocide, a legal procedure design to erase the identity of oppressed people. A law that weakens a nation's language, religion, culture, and history cannot be called unity. Unity cannot be imposed through assimilation. Unity cannot be manufactured through fear. Unity without freedom is not unity at all.

"For almost seven decades, the so-called Chinese Communist government has attempted to suppress and silence Tibetans inside Tibet and across the world. Military occupation, surveillance, imprisonment, propaganda, misinformation, disinformation campaigns, and enormous financial investment to reshape historical narratives, But failed to extinguish the Tibetan people's aspiration for freedom.

"Despite immense pressure, Tibetans have not disappeared. They have become more resilient. Every attempt to erase our identity has strengthened our determination to preserve it. Every effort to silence us has inspired new voices to speak. Every sacrifice has produced a new generation committed to carrying forward the cause of Tibet.

"The oppressor dream of creating "one big China" through coercion will remain only that a dream. so as long as Tibetans continue to preserve their national identity and seek justice. Ideas cannot be imprisoned. History cannot be rewritten simply through repetition. National identity cannot be erased by decree.

"Rangzen Lobga made his message unmistakably clear: "the root cause of the Tibetan issue is that Tibet lost its independence after China took control of our land."

"The Tibetan Youth Congress has never wavered in its position. We firmly stands and believe that the Tibetan people have the right to determine their own future, and our mission remains unchanged: to reclaim our country, Tibet, from the foreign occupation.

"This is perhaps one of the most important moments for the so-called Government of the People's Republic of China to resume sincere and meaningful dialogue with the Tibetan Government in Exile, Dialogue is not a sign of weakness. It is the mark of confidence. Nations secure in their legitimacy do not fear conversation. History has shown that governments can suppress protests, imprison individuals, and control information, but they cannot permanently extinguish a people's aspiration for freedom and dignity.

"The world has changed. Information travels across borders in seconds. Voices cannot be silenced as they once were. Attempts to conceal injustice face greater international scrutiny than ever before. Rangzen Lobga's sacrifice will not never be a forgotten chapter despite will be the source of motivation. It should serve as a warning that unresolved political conflicts continue to carry profound human consequences.

"We therefore call upon the so-called Government of the People's Republic of China to end its illegal occupation of Tibet and respect the Tibetan people's inherent right to self-determination.

"The Chinese government must recognize the legitimate aspiration of the Tibetan people and restore Tibet's independence. Lasting peace and stability cannot be achieved through repression, forced assimilation, or military control, but only by ending occupation and respecting the will of the Tibetan people. We urge China to choose justice over oppression, freedom over domination, and peace over continued confrontation.

"History will judge not only those who resisted oppression, but also those who had the opportunity to pursue peace and chose otherwise. Act now or regret later," the Tibetan activists of Tibetan Youth Congress said.

Dharamshala — The Chinese authorities have demolished thousands of residences of Tibetan monks and nuns in Larung Gar, the world’s largest Tibetan Buddhist institute, since 2001. The latest wave of demolitions began in mid-July and is set to destroy 1,060 dwellings of monks and nuns. These demolitions took place following the implementation of China’s new law, so-called the “Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress,” which came into effect on July 1, 2026.

According to these sources, on July 13, 2026, Chinese authorities began to demolish at least 1,060 dwellings belonging to monks and nuns at the Larung Five Sciences Buddhist Academy, better known as Larung Gar (monastery), located in Sertar County in eastern Tibet; at least six dwellings were demolished till July 15, 2026. These actions occurred following the implementation of so-called China's new “Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress” on July 1, 2026, which targets the Tibetan language, identity, culture, and religion as part of a policy of Sinicization and imposes the assimilation of Tibetans into Chinese culture through public institutions.

"The demolitions in Larung Gar began around July 13, 2026, and are being carried out at night, which is seen as a tactic by the authorities to prevent public documentation, media coverage, and satellite monitoring. As of July 15, 2026, six dwellings had been demolished, and Chinese authorities continue to destroy the residences; they have targeted at least 1,060 dwellings belonging to monks and nuns for demolition as part of this latest phase of demolitions," the sources said.

In 2001, Chinese authorities launched their first large-scale demolition and forced eviction operations at the Larung Gar Buddhist Academy, targeting thousands of monastic dwellings. Since then, the Chinese government has intermittently resumed its destruction activities, notably launching a massive demolitionoperationin July 2016 that reportedly resulted in theexpulsionof more than 4,800 monks and nuns and the demolition of 4,700 dwellings; the most recent wave targeted at least 1,060 dwellings.

The the Serta Larung Five Science Buddhist Academy was founded by Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok, Tibetan lama and great scholar in 1980 and has grown to the point where, it hosts between 10,000 and 40,000 residents. It is home to monks, nuns, and students from Tibet and China, as well as from other countries such as South Korea, Singapore, and Malaysia, while tens of thousands of people around the world study Buddhism through online courses taught by Sodargye Rinpoche, a prominent khenpo from Larung Gar. Despite the restrictions imposed by Chinese authorities on Tibetan Buddhism under Chinese occupation, Larung Gar has greatly contributed to the spread of this religion as well as to the preservation and international dissemination of Tibetan culture. Hundreds of eminent Buddhist scholars and practitioners have been educated at Larung Gar.

Since the Chinese government began systematically demolishing Larung Gar, the European Parliament, United Nations special rapporteurs, numerous countries, and human rights organisations, including Human Rights have officially condemned the Chinese government’s destruction of Larung Gar and called on it to put an end to these demolitions.

"China’s actions, in no doubts, constitute a gross violation of international human rights law, as well as its own Constitution, which obligates China to respect and protect the cultural, social, and religious rights of the Tibetan people. Instead, by forcing mass evictions of Tibetan monastic communities and replacing Tibetan self-governance with direct Chinese Communist Party administration, China is actively dismantling the very fabric of Tibetan life. The human toll of the Larung Gar crackdown that took place in 2016 and 2017 has been disastrous, resulting in profound psychological trauma and tragic suicides, such as the deaths of Tibetan nuns Tsering Dolma and Semgha amid the 2016 demolitions," the UN, EU, and the Human Rights Desk, Tibet Advocacy Section, DIIR, Central Tibetan Administration said.

China-Tibet: The one-thing you need to know:

Over the past 70 decades, there has been ongoing political repression, social discrimination, economic marginalization, environmental destruction, and cultural assimilation, particularly due to Chinese migration to Tibet which is fueling intense resentment among the people of occupied Tibet.

The communist-totalitarian state of China began its invasion of Tibet in 1949, reaching complete occupation of the country in 1959. Since that time, more than 1.2 million people, 20% of the nation's population of six million, have died as a direct result of China's invasion and occupation. In addition, over 99% of Tibet's six thousand religious monasteries, temples, and shrines, have been looted or decimated resulting in the destruction of hundreds of thousands of sacred Buddhist scriptures.

Until 1949, Tibet was an independent Buddhist nation in the Himalayas which had little contact with the rest of the world. It existed as a rich cultural storehouse of the Mahayana and Vajrayana teachings of Buddhism. Religion was a unifying theme among the Tibetans -- as was their own language, literature, art, and world view developed by living at high altitudes, under harsh conditions, in a balance with their environment.

He carried out this act to protest the Chinese government's repressive policies in Tibet and to demand independence for Tibet.

On June 5, 2026, a mass protest by Tibetans took place in front of the United Nations headquarters in New York—the site where Tibetan patriot Lobga Rangzen had set himself on fire to protest the Chinese government's repression of the Tibetan people, language, religion, and culture—to demand independence for Tibet, June 2,2026.

Tibetans also held a memorial service for Lobga Rangzen at the Tibetan Community Center in New York, followed by his funeral on June 6, 2026. All the Tibetans present were deeply saddened and overcome with grief by the passing of Lobga Rangzen, an independence activist of Tibet.

Sikyong Penpa Tsering of the Central Tibetan Administration expressed deep sorrow over the self-immolation of a Tibetan activist, Lobga Rangzen (Lobsang Palden), in front of the UN Headquarters in New York City on 2 July 2026.

Sikyong said,"I am deeply saddened by the devastating news of Lobga Rangzen's (Lobsang Palden) self-immolation in front of the UN Headquarters in New York City on July 2, 2026. In a video message posted hours prior, he made it clear that this ultimate sacrifice was undertaken for the Tibetan national cause. While we honor his devotion, human life is precious and must be preserved to serve the long-term struggle for Tibet."

"On behalf of the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA), I earnestly urge all fellow Tibetans to cherish your lives. The unfolding genocide inside Tibet and the enforcement of the draconian "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law" on July 1 are what drove Lobga Rangzen la to this tragic decision. He joins at least 157 Tibetans inside Tibet who have offered their lives to draw global attention to the brutal repression endured under Chinese rule," Sikyong said.

"Our deepest condolences go out to Lobga Rangzen la's family, friends, and the entire Tibetan community. On behalf of the CTA and the Tibetan people, I solemnly pledge that we will carry the spirit of these sacrifices in our hearts and work relentlessly so they are not in vain. I urgently call upon Tibetans in exile, world governments, and international human rights institutions to recognize the severe crisis inside Tibet, to stand up, and to speak out at this critical moment in our history," Sikyong concluded.

United Nations Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric expressed sadness over the self-immolation that took place outside UN headquarters, emphasising that minorities—regardless of the country—must be respected and feel as part of whole.

Dharamshala — More than 60 Tibetans shaved their heads in solidarity with Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen and all those who have sacrificed their lives for a free Tibet; Lobga Rangzen had set himself on fire in front of the United Nations headquarters to protest against China's illegal occupation of Tibet, its oppressive actions in the region, and the genocidal policies implementing in Tibet.

This Head-shaving movement took place in front of United Nations headquarters, in New York, on July 30, 2026 and it is orgainsed by 19th Regional Tibetan Youth Congress of NY&NY. They said,"This act of sacrifice is a symbol of our unwavering commitment to justice, truth, and the independence of our nation. We call upon the United Nations to uphold the principles it was founded on and stand for justice. The world cannot remain silent."

They collected the shaved hair and wrote "Justice for Lobga Rangzen" to commemorate Lhogar Rangren's sacrifice for a free and independent Tibet and to seek justice for him. They also shouted slogans such as "Justice for Lhogar Rangren," "Free Tibet," "China, out of Tibet now," and "United Nations, wake up" in front of the United Nations headquarters in New York.

Following the head-shaving movement, hundreds of Tibetans gathered in front of the United Nations headquarters in New York, the site where Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen self-immolated. They protested China's forced invasion of Tibet, destruction of Tibetan Buddhist monasteries, environmental damage, and the killing of over two million Tibetans, and its continued repressive and harsh policies against Tibetans, Tibetan culture, language, freedom of expression, religion, and belief, including the arrest, torture, and imprisonment of any Tibetan exercising their basic rights.

During their protest, they held up signs that read: "UN, when will you stop being silenced by China?", "UN, how many more lives do you need?", "Tibet belongs to Tibetans, not China", "Communist China, hands off Tibet", We want an independent for Tibet", "Protect Tibet's Faith, Culture and Nation","Lobga Rangzen is a US citizen, we want justice".

Jamphel Choesang, President of 19th Regional Tibetan Youth Congress New York/New Jersey addressed the gathering and said, "Dear Tibetan brothers and sisters, Today, I stand before you not only as the President of the 19th Regional Tibetan Youth Congress New York/New Jersey, but as a fellow Tibetan whose heart carries the same hope, pain, and unwavering love for our homeland.

"Our martyrs gave everything they had for Tibet. They did not sacrifice for themselves—they sacrificed for all of us, for future generations, and for the dream of a free and independent Tibet. Their courage must never be forgotten, and their sacrifices must never be in vain.

"Our beloved Pawo Lobga Rangzen la made the ultimate sacrifice to awaken the conscience of the world and to remind us that Tibet’s struggle is far from over. His message was clear: never give up on Tibet.

"Today, I humbly call upon every Tibetan brother and sister: please stand up for our country. Join our protests whenever you can. Raise your voice for justice. Your presence matters. Every person standing together sends a powerful message that Tibet lives in our hearts and that we will never surrender our identity, our culture, or our dream of freedom.

"Let us stand united—not divided. Let us work together as one family, one community, and one nation. When we support one another with respect, compassion, and determination, there is nothing stronger than our unity.

"The responsibility to continue this movement belongs to every one of us. Whether young or old, student or professional, every effort counts. Every protest, every prayer, every act of service, and every voice raised for Tibet keeps the flame of our martyrs burning brightly.

"Let us honor Pawo Lobga Rangzen la and all our martyrs not only with words, but through our actions. Let us continue the path they showed us with courage, discipline, and unwavering commitment.

"We call upon the international community and the United Nations to hear the voices of the Tibetan people and to seek justice for Pawo Lobga Rangzen la. His sacrifice deserves to be remembered, and the Tibetan people’s aspirations deserve to be heard.

"Together, let us pledge that we will never allow our martyrs’ sacrifices to be forgotten. We will continue to stand for truth, justice, and the freedom of Tibet until the day our nation is free."

Dharamshala — Shilong-led northeast India Tibetan People's Movement held a press conference at the Guwahatu Press Club, to address the ongoing human rights crisis in Tibet, which led to the self-immolation of Tibetan activist Lobga Rangzen, in front of UN headquarters in New York, on July 2, 2026. They told the media about who is Tibetan independent activist Lobga Rangzen and why he self-immolated in front of UN headquarters in New York. They further recalled China's invasion of Tibet and denounced the Chinese government's eradication of Tibetan language, identity, culture, and religion in the name of so-called China's “Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress"; finally they rejected the law by tearing the law paper, in front of reporters.

Shilong-led northeast India Tibetan People's Movement, planned to organise a large peaceful protest in Guwahati (Assam) on July 29, 2026, to protest against China's so-called "Ethnic Unity Law" and demand freedom, justice, and respect for human rights in Tibet. Tibetans from various northeastern states—including Dimapur (Nagaland), Tawang (Arunachal Pradesh), Tezpur (Assam), Shillong (Meghalaya), and Guwahati (Assam)—were set to participate; however, due to flooding in Assam, the demonstration had to be postponed, and a press conference was held instead on the originally scheduled date of July 29, 2026.

Two former members of Tibetan Parliament-in-exile, Tsering Dolma and Yangchen Dolkar, Tenzin sangmo, media coordinator and Youndoung, secretary of Shilong-led northeast India Tibetan People's Movement held the press conference.

The statement of the Shilong-led northeast India Tibetan People's Movement said," Lobga Rangzen, a 52-year-old Tibetan activist, died after a self-immolation protest he carried out in front of the UN headquarters in New York City on July 2, 2026. He called for the restoration of Tibet's independence and spoke against the imposition of China's "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law" that went into force on July 1 in Tibet. Tibetans reject this law as it is designed to legitimise the imposition of sinicization policies in Tibet. Tibetans are not an ethnic minority of China to be subjected to its ethnic unity law in the name of unity and progress.

"In 1950, the People's Liberation Army entered Tibet, fundomentally changing the course of Tibetan history. Following the 1959 Tibetan Uprising, His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama and approximately 80,000 Tibetans fled into exile in India. Since China's military occupation of Tibet, Tibetans have lived under policies that many governments, UN experts and international human rights organisations say have severely restricted fundamental rights.

"More than 170 Tibetans have self-immolated since 2009, pealing in 2012 with 85 self-immolations in one year. All the self-immolators unanimously called for freedom in Tibet, the protection of Tibetan Identity, the return of His Holiness the Dalai lama to Tibet, and unity among Tibetans. His Holiness the 14th Dalal Lama and the exile government continue to make efforts toward peaceful resolution of the Sino-Tibetan conflict through its "Middle Way Approach". However, China has only turned a cold shoulder to the proposals and responds with rhetoric that undermines the spirit of dialogue. It has put the Tibetans in a difficult position of experiencing the worsening human rights situation in Tibet, while watching China intensify its hold on Tibet. Self-Immolations don't occur in a vacuum, but as a result of deep-seated anguish and exhaustion of tangible recourse.

"On July 1, 2026, China's "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law" come into force. According to the Chinese government, the law "promotes national unity". However, eight UN human rights experts and international human rights organisations have warned that it further institutionalizes policies affecting the linguistic, cultural and religious rights of ethnic minorities.

There are major factual inaccuracies in the law and in the UN response:

• Tibet is not part of China to be absorbed into the project of national unity• Tibetans are minoritised by the Chinese occupation and are not one of the ethnic minority groups China claims to constitute.• China is ethnically Han Chinese dominated, with no historical, cultural, racial, linguistic or political association with the Tibetans, except as the dominast race of the colonising power.

"On the ground in Tibet, the law has real time impact on education, language, religion and cultural rights as it mandates cultural integration. The single Chinese national identity it promotes includes provisions with extraterritorial application, raising concerns that it could exacerbate the patterns of transnational repression against individuals and organisations globally. For many Tibetans, the law is seen not as a new policy but as the formal codification of decades of assimilation measures through instrumentalisation of law.

"Why should India and northeast care for Tibet. The Tibetan Plateau forms much of the strategic frontier between India and China. Since China's occupation of Tibet, the Himalayan region has become one of Asia's most heavily militarised borders. China has escalated its territorial claims over Arunachal Pradesh, referring to it as "South Tibet," and maintains unresolved border disputes with India in eastern Ladakh. These disputes have contributed to recurring military tensions, including the 2020 Galwan Valley clash.

"For the people of Northeast India, Tibet is not only a human rights issue—it is also an environmental and regional concern.
