title: His Holiness the Dalai Lama congratulates Andy Burnham, the new PM of the UK - Tibet Post International
content:
Dharamshala — His Holiness the Dalai Lama congratulated Andy Burnham on his assumption of the office of Prime Minister of the UK. His Holiness wrote, "I wish you every success in meeting the challenges that lie ahead in fulfilling the needs and aspirations of the British people, and in contributing to the creation of a more peaceful and compassionate world for us all."
His Holiness the Dalai Lama wrote to Andy Burnham on July 21, 2026, from the Shewatsel Phodrang in Leh, Ladakh (India), to congratulate him on taking office as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom. Andy Burnham assumed office as the 57th Prime Minister of the United Kingdom on July 20, 2026, after meeting with King Charles III at Buckingham Palace to form a new government, succeeding Sir Keir Starmer.
His Holiness the Dalai Lama wrote,"Today, the world is passing through a very difficult and uncertain time. Historically, your country has played a leadership role in international affairs, and it is my hope that even as you work for the development of your own nation, you will also work closely with other countries to resolve the problems before us — both urgent and long-term — with a firm belief in the oneness of humanity and a shared desire for peace and happiness."
The spiritual leader of Tibet said, “As you may be aware, we Tibetans have long enjoyed a historic and unique relationship with your country. During my several visits there, I have deeply appreciated the warmth extended to me by people from all walks of life, as well as their support for my efforts to promote human values, nonviolence, and interfaith harmony.”
“I wish you every success in meeting the challenges that lie ahead in fulfilling the needs and aspirations of the British people, and in contributing to the creation of a more peaceful and compassionate world for us all,"His Holiness concluded his congratulatory letter.

title: Thousands of Tibetans staged protest to condenm PRC's "Ethic Unity Law" - Tibet Post International
content:
Dharamshala — Thousands of Tibetans staged a strong protest against the Chinese government’s repressive policies in Tibet, particular to China's so-called "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law" and they said, "this law is an illegal instrument to institutionalize the Chinese government's long-standing policy of forced assimilation and to strengthen state control over non-Chinese peoples, particularly Tibetans." They also expressed solidarity with Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen, who self-immolated to protest against the PRC's oppressive policies in Tibet and to demand independence for Tibet.
The Tibetan Youth Congress, the Tibetan Women's Association, Students for a Free Tibet – India, Gu-Chu-Sum Movement of Tibet, National Democratic Party of Tibet, and the International Tibet Network, organised a joint protest honoring the supreme sacrifice of Martyr Lobga Rangzen and condemning China's so-called "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law." The protest joined by thousands of Tibetans around the Dharamshala and they marched from McLeod Ganj to Kachari, Dharamshala, on July 18, 2026.
The Tibetan organisations and protestors call on the United Nations and the international community to recognise martyr Lobga Rangzen's sacrifice, address the worsening human rights situation in Tibet, reject China's policy of forced assimilation, and support the Tibetan people's right to freedom.
When Tibetan protestors marching from gate of Tsuklakhang, Mecleod to Police Groud, Kacheri, Dharamshala, they carried Lobga Rangzen’s coffin and protested against the Chinese government's repressive policies in Tibet. They chanted slogans such as: "UNO, wake up," "UNO, speak for Tibet," "World leaders, wake up," "World leaders, speak up for Tibet," "China lies, Tibetans die," "We want justice for Lobga Rangzen," "Lobga Rangzen’s life matters," "Lobga Rangzen died for a free Tibet," "We want justice for Tibetans," "Shame on the UNO," "China is guilty, guilty of genocide," and "Stop the cultural genocide in Tibet."
Tsering Dolma, President of Tibetan Women's Association read out the statement of above Tibetan NGOs in English, she said, "Recent on July 2, 2026, Tibetan patriot Lobga Rangzen set himself on fire in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York in a profound act of sacrifice for Tibet and its people. In his final video testament, he made clear that his action was not driven by personal despair, but by his deep concern for the survival of the Tibetan nation. He warned that the Chinese government is carrying out policies aimed at destroying the Tibetan people through systematic repression and the eradication of Tibetan identity."
"Lobga Rangzen emphasized that no nation has ever succeeded without commitment, courage, and action for freedom movement. He appealed to Tibetans everywhere to unite and work on the common cause of Tibet's independence. In his testament, Lobga Rangzen stated that we Tibetans lost our fundamental rights and freedoms because we lost our country Tibet. He called upon the Tibetan Government in Exile, the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, Tibetan civil society organisations, and Tibetans around the world to unite and work collectively for the future of Tibet," she added.
"He also requested that his sacrifice should not lead to the cancellation of cultural performances, songs, or other expressions of Tibetan identity, emphasizing that these are essential to preserving Tibetan culture and inspiring younger generations. He asked Tibetans not to mourn his death but instead to fulfill the aspirations for which he sacrificed his life. His final words were: "Victory to Tibet! Victory for Tibet’s Independence!"
Tsering Chophel, President of Tibetan Youth Congress said,"On March 12, 2026, during the National People's Congress, the Chinese Communist government adopted the so-called “Regulations on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress”, a 65-article law that entered into force on July 1,2026, coinciding with the anniversary of the founding of the Chinese Communist Party. Presented under the language of "ethnic unity," this law is an illegal instrument to institutionalize the Chinese government's long-standing policy of forced assimilation and to strengthen state control over non-Chinese peoples, particularly Tibetans.
"The implementation of this law represents a serious escalation of China's efforts to erase the distinct identity of the Tibetan people. Through the systematic assimilation of language, religion, culture, customs, history, and education, it seeks to transform Tibet into an inseparable part of a single Chinese national identity, thereby undermining the Tibetan people's fundamental rights, dignity, and national identity. In response to these developments, the Tibetan NGOs and support group jointly issue the following demands to the Chinese government, the United Nations, and the international community:
1. United Nations Response: As Lobga Rangzen made the ultimate sacrifice in front of the United Nations Headquarters, we urge the United Nations to respond in a meaningful and formal manner by addressing the grave human rights situation in Tibet and the circumstances that compelled his sacrifice.
2. Accountability for Tibetans Driven to Self-Immolation: The Chinese government must be held accountable for the policies and repression that have driven Lobga Rangzen and numerous Tibetans to the tragic act of self-immolation.
3. Recognition of Tibet's Sovereignty: Tibet was an independent nation before its occupation by the so called People's Republic of China and remains under Chinese occupation today. We call upon the international community to recognize Tibet's historical status and support the Tibetan people's right to restore their freedom and independence.
4. Repeal the so-called “Ethnic Unity and Progress Law”: We reject this law as an instrument of forced assimilation and call for its immediate repeal and the cessation of its implementation throughout Tibet.
5. International Action and Monitoring: We call upon governments, international organisations, and human rights mechanisms to closely monitor the implementation of the so-called “Ethnic Unity and Progress law”, investigate its impact on Tibetans and other peoples under Chinese rule, and hold the so-called People's Republic of China accountable under international human rights standards.
Tenzing Pasang, National Director of Students for a Free Tibet said, "We reject and condemn the recent statement made by Mr Stéphane Dujarric, spokesperson of the Secretary-General (United Nations) referring to Tibet as a "minority." Such characterization is historically inaccurate, politically misleading, and serves only to reinforce the Chinese Communist Party's propaganda. Tibet is not a minority of China. It is an occupied nation with its own distinct history, civilization, language, culture, religion, government, and national identity. Calling Tibet a "minority" erases its national identity and undermines the Tibetan people's right to freedom and independence.
"We call on the United Nations to uphold truth and impartiality. It must not use language that legitimizes China's occupation of Tibet or erases the Tibetan nation's identity. The United Nations' words shape global opinion. They must not legitimize occupation or contribute to the erasure of Tibet's identity and the Tibetan people's aspirations for freedom," she concluded.

title: Tibetan Youth Congress Launches a Global Series of Protests Against PRC - Tibet Post International
content:
Dharamshala — Tibetan Youth Congress launchesd a Worldwide Chain Protest in Memory of Martyr Lobga Rangzen and Rejects China's so-called "Ethnic Unity Law" on Sunday. They said," The law provides a legal framework for enforcing political conformity and accelerating the assimilation of peoples living under Chinese occupation and rule, including Tibet, East Turkistan, Southern Mongolia, and Manchuria. Unity cannot be created through coercion."
The Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) launched of a Worldwide Chain Protest in Memory of Martyr Lobga Rangzen and Rejects China's so-called "Ethnic Unity and progressive Law", beginning from Dharamshala on July 19, 2026 and expanding across the globe through our regional chapters and supporters, nearly 20 countries across the world.
The first group of people participating in the hunger strike includes Lobsang Tsering, Gonpo Dhondup, Karma Yeshe, Lobsang Yeshe, Tenzin Lhamo, and Penpa Tsering—all former members of the executive committee of the Central Tibetan Youth Congress.The TYC will organise a month-long hunger strike in Dharamsala, after which its members will travel to New Delhi and other locations where the regional TYC existed. Furthermore, the Worldwide Chain Protest in Memory of Martyr Lobga Rangzen and Rejects China's so-called "Ethnic Unity and progressive Law", — will take place in New York and at various locations across the United States, Canada, Europe, and other countries to continue the campaign.
Tenzin Lobsang, general secretary of TYC read out the statement of TYC and said, "This international campaign honors the life and final appeal of Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen, who died following his self-imolation protest outside of United Nations Headquarters in New York, on July 2, 2026.
"Lobga Rangzen devoted his life to the Tibetan freedom movement. His death must not be reduced to a passing tragedy or met only with words of condolence. His final protest was an appeal to the conscience of the international community and a reminder that Tibet remains an occupied nation whose people continue to struggle for freedom and independence.
"His appeal cannot be ignored, buried, or erased. The Tibetan Youth Congress will carry his message forward through sustained, collective, and nonviolent action until the Tibetan people's struggle receives the international attention and action it demands.
"Beginning in Dharamshala, TYC will organise a chain hunger strike accompanied by coordinated demonstrations, candlelight vigils, public rallies, awareness campaigns, diplomatic outreach, and peaceful direct actions. TYC chapters and supporters worldwide will continue these actions in succession, standing together unity, and resistance."
Tashi Dharjee, Vice President of TYC said, "The Tibetan Youth Congress unequivocally rejects the "Ethnic Unity and Progress Promotion Law" imposed by the so-called People's Republic of China. The law, which came into force on July 1, 2026, provides a legal framework for enforcing political conformity and accelerating the assimilation of peoples living under Chinese occupation and rule, including Tibet, East Turkistan, Southern Mongolia, and Manchuria.
"Unity cannot be created through coercion. Behind the language of "ethnic unity", this law strengthens a unilateral system through, which the Chinese government suppresses distinct languages, dominates religious institutions, rewrites history, destroys cultural hentage, separates children from their families and communities through state-run colonial boardino schools, and demands absolute loyalty to the Chinese Communist Party.
"A government cannot legislate away the identity of a nation. A policy intended to erase a people's language, culture, history, and spiritual heritage is not unity. It is state-enforced assimilation."
TYC activists said, "in response to the self-immolation of Martyr Lobga Rangzen, the continuing occupation of Tibet, and the implementation of China's assimilation law, the Tibetan Youth Congress issues the following demands:
1. A formal and substantive response from the United Nations: Lobga Rangzen carried out his final protest outside the United Nations Headquarters. The United Nations must respond with more than condolences. We call upon the Secretary-General, the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, and relevant UN mechanisms to formally address the human rights crisis in Tibet and the circumstances that led to his protest. The United Nations must press China to grant meaningful and unfettered access to Tibet for UN experts, independent observers, and international journalists.
2. An end to language that erases Tibet's national identity: We reject the framing used by Stéphane Dujarric, Spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General, which treated the Tibetan people merely as a "minority" within China.
Such language is historically inaccurate and politically consequential. It reinforces the Chinese Communist Party's narrative, erases Tibet's independent national identity, and undermines the Tibetan people's right to freedom and independence. The United Nations must uphold truth and impartiality. Its language must not legitimize China's occupation or prejudge the political status and aspirations of the Tibetan people.
3. Accountability for the repression that has driven Tibetans to self-immolation: The Chinese government must be held accountable for the policies and repression that have created the conditions in which LobgaRangzen and numerous other Tibetans have resorted to the act of self-immolation.
We call upon the United Nations and governments worldwide to investigate, document, and publicly challenge China's violations of the political, cultural, linguistic, and religious rights of the Tibetan people.
4. Recognition of Tibet's sovereignty and right to independence: Tibet was an independent nation before its occupation by the People's Republic of China and remains under Chinese occupation today.
We call upon goverments, parliaments, and intermational institutions to recognize Tibet's historical status, reject the characterization of Tibet as merely an internal matter of China, and support the Tibetan people's right to restore their freedom and independence.
5. Immediate repeal of the so-called Ethnic Unity and Progress Promotion Law: We reject immediately repeal it, halt its implementation throughout Tibet, and end all policies intended to eliminate Tibet's distinct national, linguistic, cultural, and religious identity.
6. The immediate and unconditional release of all Tibetan political prisoners: We demand the inmediate and unconditional release of the 1l th Panchen Lama, who became the world's youngest political prisoners after being taken into Chinese custody as a child.
We further demand the release of all Tibetan political prisoners including environmental activists, artists, writers, religious figures, and others imprisoned for peacefully defending Tibet's land, identity, culture, religion, language, and freedom.
Lobga Rangzen's death does not mark the end of his struggle. It is a renewed call for resistance, solidarity, and international action. It confronts the world with a choice: continued silence in the face of occupation and forced assimilation, or meaningful action in defense of truth, freedom, and justice.
The United Nations cannot remain a silent witness. Governments cannot continue to treat Tibet as an inconvenient issue to be ignored. Silence enables repression, and inaction allows the destruction of a nation to continue.
Lobga Rangzen's courage has become a symbol of the unbreakable Tibetan spirit. We honor Lobga Rangzen's life by amplifying his voice through our movement, our unity, and our unwavering commitment to Tibet's independence."
